where: Section 2 (dark current paragraph) and Quiz Q7
problem: It says both parts of the dark current are multiplied by M in an APD. Standard photodiode theory splits dark current into a bulk part, which does see the avalanche gain, and a surface-leakage part, which does not see the gain because it bypasses the multiplication region. The quiz answer repeats the same wrong claim, so a student would lose marks and would also over-estimate APD noise.
fix: Dark current has a bulk part, proportional to the depleted volume, and a surface leakage part. Only the bulk part is multiplied by M in an APD; the surface part adds directly. Write Id = M·Idb + Ids, with Idb the bulk part in A, Ids the surface part in A, and M the gain. Update the Q7 answer to the same wording.

problem: The formula gives σrms the unit of amperes, but NEP is then said to be in W/√Hz. With σrms in A, σrms/R comes out in W, not W/√Hz. The unit is right only if the noise current is a spectral density in A/√Hz, that is, noise per 1 Hz of bandwidth.
fix: State that σrms here is the rms noise current per unit bandwidth, in A/√Hz, so NEP = σrms/R is in W/√Hz. In Q6 add the same clarification: NEP is the optical power giving SNR = 1 in a 1 Hz bandwidth.

problem: The note on the output node reads 'Iph / σ', an amplitude ratio, but the text defines SNR as the power ratio Iph²/σ². A student may copy the wrong ratio into the exam.

The total noise is written 'σ² = ish2 + ith2', with plain digits instead of superscripts and without the subscript markup used in the rest of the chapter. It reads like a different quantity from ish² and ith².
fix: Write σ² = ish² + ith² using the same sub/sup formatting as the displayed noise formulas.
